DuckDB: my favourite tool for data work

The problem it solves

Data comes as files: CSV, Parquet, JSONL. Too big for Excel, too small to justify a database server. Loading everything into pandas eats memory and time, and setting up Postgres just to answer a question is overkill. Meanwhile SQL is the best language for most questions about data.

The general idea

DuckDB is an analytical SQL database that runs inside your process. There is no server: it is a single binary or a Python library, it queries files where they are, it is columnar and very fast, and a whole database is a single file. It is my favourite tool, because it is the shortest path from a file to an answer.

Examples

Query files directly, with no import step:

SELECT city, avg(price)
FROM 'prices.parquet'
GROUP BY city
ORDER BY 2 DESC;

SELECT count(*) FROM read_json_auto('events.jsonl');
COPY (SELECT * FROM 'rents.csv') TO 'rents.parquet';

And from Python, with the result as a dataframe:

import duckdb

df = duckdb.sql("SELECT * FROM 'prices.parquet' WHERE rooms >= 3").df()

Tips from my setup

Here is how it looks in one of my projects, a data pipeline with a model on top:

  • One database file, organised in schemas. The project keeps a single bwf.duckdb with raw, features and models layers, and the SQL that builds each layer lives in versioned .sql files in the repository.
  • Recipes for the pipeline. just refresh pulls and loads the new data, just rebuild-db builds the database again from scratch, and just export-features hands the feature tables to the models. just load-jsonl source table loads any JSONL file into a table.
  • A read-only monitoring session. just db opens DuckDB with an init script that attaches the database as READ_ONLY and prints a freshness overview of the tables. Because it only reads, it never blocks the running app, and DuckDB's single-writer rule is respected.
  • DuckDB everywhere else. yazi opens a .duckdb file in the shell on Enter, Neovim sends SQL to a DuckDB REPL, and marimo has SQL cells on top of the same file. See those posts.
  • Rules for my agents. My Claude instructions say to read data files with DuckDB, to open .duckdb files read-only and never to modify the source data.
